counterfactual_missing_items: No histopathologic confirmation of granulomas is available
No flushing, telangiectasias, or ocular symptoms are described
No classic PG ulcer with violaceous undermined border is described
decisive_items: multiple papules and pustules on an erythematous base over the nasal dorsum, some with superficial ulceration and yellow crusting
He had been treated with systemic and topical antibiotics at a local hospital without improvement
He denied fever, cough, joint pain, or other systemic symptoms
response.rationale: R1 best explains the full composite: papulopustular erythematous nasal eruption with superficial ulceration/crusting, absence of systemic symptoms, and antibiotic-refractory course. R4 matches the erythematous papulopustular nasal component but not the ulceration/crusting or antibiotic failure. R3/C1 are nonspecific and contradicted by antibiotic failure; R5 lacks pustular/crusting features; R2 lacks a classic PG ulcer and has an atypical nasal location.

rejected.why: PG requires a characteristic ulcer with violaceous undermined border; nasal papulopustular eruption without systemic association is atypical.
Folliculitis is nonspecific and would be expected to improve with antibiotics; ulceration/crusting and antibiotic failure are unexplained.
Redundant append-only completion of R3 with no independent raw support; adds only anatomy without changing diagnosis.
Sarcoidosis does not explain pustules and crusting; no systemic or lymph node findings support it.
